subject: an example for the Log Guassian Cox Process when data are counts?

messages.author: f6d7dbf40606191a
messages.subject: an example for the Log Guassian Cox Process when data are counts?
parts:
Hello,

I have a dataset obtained from a crop field divided into quadrats. Some quadrats are sampled and in these quadrats a count of the number of plants is observed
it is not clear to me if with INLA I can estimate the parameters of a Log Gaussian Cox Process based on such data: observation of counts (i.e.not directly plant positions) on a sample of the quadrats (as opposed to all quadrats).
I can see articles dealing with using INLA for the LGCP but the data set seem different.

Thank you in advance for your help!

messages.author: bbb9357156c132fe
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] an example for the Log Guassian Cox Process when data are counts?
parts:
Hi Nathalie,

Yes it can.   Fitting LGCPs from quadrat count data is covered in this paper: http://projecteuclid.org/euclid.aoas/1356629049

In order to deal with only a subset ofquadrats being sampled, simple tell INLA that the "expected number" of quadrats (E in the inla call) is zero in these cells.

result = inla( ..., E = <1 for sampled quadrates, zero for unsampled quadrats>, ...)

Best wishes,

Dan
